title: Taurine chloramine inhibits functional responses of human eosinophilsin vitro

sections.abstract: <jats:title>Summary</jats:title><jats:p><jats:bold>Background</jats:bold>Eosinophils are prominent effectors of allergic inflammation. Taurine‐chloramine (TauCl), a derivative of the amino acid taurine, shows antioxidant properties in different cell systems but its effects on eosinophils have not been reported.</jats:p><jats:p><jats:bold>Objective</jats:bold>To study the effects of TauCl and taurine on functional responses of isolated human eosinophils activated by different stimuli.</jats:p><jats:p><jats:bold>Methods</jats:bold>Human eosinophils were purified from the blood of healthy donors by a magnetic bead separation system. The effects of TauCl and taurine (0.1–1 m<jats:sc>m</jats:sc>) were investigated on the generation of superoxide anion (ferricytochrome‐<jats:italic>c</jats:italic>reduction microassay), calcium signal (fluorimetry), p47<jats:sup>phox</jats:sup>–p67<jats:sup>phox</jats:sup>translocation (Western blot), leukotriene C<jats:sub>4</jats:sub>(LTC<jats:sub>4</jats:sub>) production (enzymeimmunoassay), eosinophil peroxidase (EPO) release (spectrophotometry), eosinophil cationic protein (ECP) release (radioimmunoassay), apoptosis (flow cytometry with annexin V‐propidium iodide), and nuclear factor‐κB (NF‐κB) activation (Western blot).</jats:p><jats:p><jats:bold>Results</jats:bold>TauCl inhibited superoxide anion generation triggered by<jats:italic>N</jats:italic>‐formyl‐Met–Leu–Phe (fMLP; 30 n<jats:sc>m</jats:sc>), phorbol myristate acetate (1 n<jats:sc>m</jats:sc>) and serum opsonized zymosan (0.5 mg/mL) with similar potency (IC<jats:sub>50</jats:sub>∼200 μ<jats:sc>m</jats:sc>) for the three stimuli, while taurine (0.1–1 m<jats:sc>m</jats:sc>) was scarcely effective. TauCl but not taurine inhibited p47<jats:sup>phox</jats:sup>–p67<jats:sup>phox</jats:sup>translocation. TauCl (200 μ<jats:sc>m</jats:sc>) and taurine (1 m<jats:sc>m</jats:sc>) did not modify the [Ca<jats:sup>2+</jats:sup>]<jats:sub>i</jats:sub>responses to fMLP. TauCl inhibited the release of EPO (IC<jats:sub>50</jats:sub>∼200 μ<jats:sc>m</jats:sc>) and reduced ECP and LTC<jats:sub>4</jats:sub>production from fMLP‐activated eosinophils while taurine was without significant effects. TauCl (1 m<jats:sc>m</jats:sc>) did not change constitutive apoptosis but significantly attenuated the ability of granulocyte‐monocyte colony‐stimulating factor (GM‐CSF) and IL‐5 to prevent apoptosis. The activation of eosinophil NF‐κB induced by GM‐CSF and IL‐5 was suppressed by TauCl.</jats:p><jats:p><jats:bold>Conclusion</jats:bold>Taurine is without significant<jats:italic>in vitro</jats:italic>effects on human eosinophil functions but its derivative TauCl inhibits oxidative burst and generation of inflammatory mediators, and reverses the survival effect produced by inflammatory cytokines. Therefore, endogenous TauCl may help to suppress excessive inflammatory response in eosinophils at inflammatory sites.</jats:p>
